- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast slightly to account for risk aversion or panic-driven volatility.
- Model consistently over-forecasts early in the 30-day horizon (days 1–5) — especially after spikes — and under-forecasts late (days 25–30); apply smoothing or decay to later days.
- After a price spike (e.g., >2.0), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; cap forecast at 1.5–2.0x the spike peak for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in the last 5–7 days; if forecast is >1.5x recent mean, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) correlates with forecast error — when sentiment shifts sharply, model lags by 1–2 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
